name: Cambered Bar Bench Press
description: The Cambered Bar Bench Press uses a specialty bar with the bar sleeves suspended below the main grip section by a curved or cambered frame. When pressing, the bar hangs several inches below the grip, allowing the elbows to drop lower than the bench surface and providing a greater pectoral stretch at the bottom of the movement than is achievable with a standard straight barbell.

execution.starting_position: Load the cambered bar on the rack. The swinging pendulum effect means the bar is inherently unstable. Grip firmly and establish upper back contact with the bench before unracking.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the rack hooks to accommodate the cambered bar's height. Due to the bar drop, hooks will need to be set higher than for a standard bench press. Test the swing of the bar before loading heavily.
steps: Step 1: Unrack and control the pendulum sway of the bar.
Step 2: Lower under control — the elbows drop below the bench level, creating deep pectoral stretch.
Step 3: Press up from the deep stretched position.
Step 4: Reach full lockout, controlling bar sway throughout.
execution.breathing_instructions: Deep breath and brace before lowering. Hold through the deep stretch position. Exhale on press.
common_mistakes: Panicking at the instability and rushing through the bottom position
Not adjusting rack height to account for the dropped sleeve position
safety_considerations: The swinging of the loaded sleeves creates unpredictable movement — reduce load significantly from your standard bench max
Use a power rack with spotter arms
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Deeper than a standard bench press. Allow elbows to descend fully below the bench surface.
coaching_cues: Feel the deep pec stretch at the bottom before pressing
